summary.headline: Sai Life Q2 FY27 revenue grew 23% YoY to lead with 28% EBITDA margin; 225 KL Bidar capacity ready, second 225 KL block slipped to Q3 FY28.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 23% YoY, with CDMO up 20% and CRO up 28%. H1 FY27 revenue grew 17% YoY, with CRO at 38% and CDMO at 62% of H1 revenue. EBITDA margin was 28% in both Q2 and H1, and management reiterated that H2 will be stronger than H1. Management said it added one molecule to late-phase and moved one molecule from late-phase to commercial, and it cited Middle East-driven solvent and chemical cost pressure with recovery efforts underway. The second 225 KL CDMO block was pushed from Q4 FY27 to Q3 FY28 to prioritise capacity for large pharma customers.

financial_highlights.metric: CRO share of H1 FY27 revenue
CDMO share of H1 FY27 revenue

segments.name: CRO (discovery and integrated services)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue grew 28% YoY and CRO contributed 38% of H1 FY27 revenue. Management attributed growth to integrated discovery with existing customers and to rising large pharma presence, with pharma at 40% of the CRO split.

segments.name: CDMO (development and commercial manufacturing)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue grew 20% YoY and CDMO contributed 62% of H1 FY27 revenue. Late-phase pipeline stood at 14 programmes and commercial at 34 molecules, with one molecule moving from late-phase to commercial in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1 FY27; management declined to give a H2 revenue split, saying visibility is good.
Full-year FY27 capex plan of INR1,100-1,300 crores reiterated, with H1 spend of INR621 crores.
Bidar expanded small molecule capacity of around 220 KL is ready; final quality trials underway before commercial batches, expected to be revenue accretive this year.
Second 225 KL capacity now due in Q3 FY28, versus Q4 FY27 earlier; management said this does not affect FY28 revenue commitments.

Telangana greenfield site expected to break ground in Q4 FY27 (later clarified as January-February); management said a strong capex cycle is expected over the next couple of years, but gave no three-to-four-year capex guidance.
Management said it remains confident in long-term growth and EBITDA projections, but declined to guide on CRO headcount, integrated partnership revenue, or wallet share.
capex_capacity: Bidar: around 220 KL expanded small molecule capacity is ready, with final quality trials underway.
Second capacity phase: 225 KL block moved from Q4 FY27 to Q3 FY28 to prioritise capability needed by large pharma customers.
Peptide development lab commissioned; additional peptide development labs under construction, expected in the next few months; Class 6 containment labs for ADC and peptide development expected soon.

Plant utilisation: management said a CDMO plant is considered fully utilised at around 70-75%; Q2 utilisation cited by an analyst at 67%. Capacity decisions are taken 24-36 months ahead, and management said no plant has a complete customer commitment.
Funding: management said leverage is comfortable and it will not starve the business of capex, with debt or market raises possible if needed.
demand_pricing: Integrated outsourcing: one large pharma relationship moved into operations, and a second large pharma was converted into a similar strategic engagement; management is in talks with more large pharma companies.
Integrated discovery programmes started with two large pharma customers; management described these as small today.
Biotech enquiries rose, many for integrated engagements in peptides; management said biotech funding is in a mid-cycle phase and expected to recover.
Middle East situation raised costs of certain solvents and chemicals; management is working with customers to recover incremental costs.
Large pharma count is 19 of 25 top customers; largest customer was about 12% of revenue as of end of last year.

qa_highlights.question: How much of CRO growth comes from capacity, headcount, discovery versus chemistry, or new customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited integrated discovery with existing customers and growth in large pharma; pharma is 40% of the CRO split. Headcount is about 4,400 at end-September. No CRO growth outlook was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the active NCE count stay at 34, and does the CRO block at 85-90% utilisation mean more CRO capex?
qa_highlights.answer: The 34 count reflects a typo fix from 33, with one molecule becoming less active and one moving from late-phase to commercial. Management said CRO capacity is already being added.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the customer concentration risk from the new integrated programmes?
qa_highlights.answer: The largest customer was about 12% of revenue. Management said integrated, multi-service relationships reduce per-product concentration, and it has onboarded two new large pharma customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation, customer commitment and breakeven timeline for new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a CDMO plant is fully utilised at around 70-75%, that capacity is decided 24-36 months ahead, and that no plant has complete customer commitment. It did not give a breakeven timeline.

qa_highlights.question: How will capex be funded given cash near INR100 crores and internal accruals of INR400-500 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said leverage is comfortable and it will use it; it did not give a full funding plan but said debt or fresh market raises are possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the 225 KL capacity delayed, and what is the H1/H2 revenue split?
qa_highlights.answer: A large pharma needed other capability more urgently, so it was prioritised; the block moves from Q4 FY27 to Q3 FY28. Management said H2 visibility is good but declined to give a number.

risks_watch: Second 225 KL capacity delayed to Q3 FY28, which could affect FY28 revenue if demand moves faster.
Middle East-linked solvent and chemical cost pressure; recovery from customers is not yet confirmed in amount or timing.
Integrated partnerships are early-stage; timing, scope and revenue of the second engagement are not disclosed and management said outcomes may not mature.
Customer concentration: largest customer about 12% of revenue; management expects top-10 rankings to shift over two to three years.
Talent remains a challenge per management; senior and mid-level turnover described as very low.
Funding path for the INR1,100-1,300 crore capex plan and the upcoming Telangana site is not fully defined.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and integrated-model traction, but guarded on timing: management repeatedly declined to give timelines, guidance or numbers on pipeline conversion, H2 split and partnership revenue, and recalibrated the 225 KL capacity date.
key_quotes: As we conclude another successful quarter for the company, our priorities at Sai remain unchanged: to deepen our relationships with global pharmaceutical companies, expand the range and complexity of services we offer, and build the capacity and capabilities required to support customers over the long term.
We do not expect this change in timelines to affect our ability to meet our revenue commitments in fiscal '28.

This business is a service business unless you put up capacity and unless you're available and be ready, customers will move up their products from a clinical phase to some other supplier in commercial.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 67% (below the 70-75% full point) and the Telangana greenfield site is expected to break ground in January-February 2027, with the FY27 capex plan of INR1,100-1,300 crore reiterated and INR621 crore spent in H1; no three-to-four-year capex guidance was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The 225 KL block slipped a quarter (Q4 FY27 to Q3 FY28), Middle East cost recovery is unconfirmed in amount or timing, and funding for the INR1,100-1,300 crore capex plan is not fully defined.

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: Integrated large-pharma engagements
rows.why: One large pharma moved into operations and a second was converted to a strategic engagement, with talks ongoing with more large pharma, but management said the programmes are small today and revenue timing is undisclosed.

rows.label: Middle East cost recovery from customers
rows.why: Solvent and chemical costs rose from the Middle East situation and management is working with customers to recover incremental costs, but neither the amount nor timing is confirmed.
